text: When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go off as before to seek omens, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam looked up and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
He took up his oracle and said: "The word of Balaam son of Beor, the word of the man whose eye is opened,
the word of one who hears the sayings of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down with eyes uncovered:
How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!
They stretch out like valleys, like gardens beside a river, like aloes planted by the LORD, like cedars beside the waters.
Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall have abundant water. His king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.
God brought him out of Egypt; he has the strength of a wild ox. He devours the nations that oppose him, breaks their bones to pieces, and shatters them with his arrows.
He crouches, he lies down like a lion, like a lioness—who dares rouse him? Blessed is everyone who blesses you, and cursed is everyone who curses you."
Then Balak's anger flared against Balaam. He struck his hands together and said to him, "I called you to curse my enemies, and look—you have blessed them three times over!
Now get out of here, back to your own place! I said I would reward you richly, but the LORD has kept you from any reward."
Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not tell the messengers you sent me:
'Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD to do anything, good or bad, of my own accord. What the LORD says, that is what I will speak'?
Now I am going back to my people, but come, let me tell you what this people will do to your people in the days to come."
Then he took up his oracle and said: "The word of Balaam son of Beor, the word of the man whose eye is opened,
the word of one who hears the sayings of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down with eyes uncovered:
I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel. He shall crush the brow of Moab and break down all the sons of Sheth.
Edom shall be his possession, and Seir, his enemy, shall be possessed, while Israel does mighty deeds.
One from Jacob shall rule, and destroy the survivors of the city."
Then Balaam looked at Amalek and took up his oracle and said: "Amalek was the first of the nations, but its end shall be destruction."

versions.text: Then Balaam looked at Amalek and took up his oracle: "Amalek was the first of the nations, but its end shall be destruction."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew formula וַיִּשָּׂא מְשָׁלוֹ וַיֹּאמַר ('took up his oracle and said') is rendered fully in vv. 3, 15, and 23 but abbreviated here (and in v. 21). Restoring 'and said' keeps the recurring refrain consistent, which matters for oral reading.

text: He looked at the Kenites and took up his oracle: "Your dwelling is secure, your nest is set in the rock;
yet Kain shall be laid waste. How long before Asshur takes you captive?

versions.text: yet Kain shall be laid waste. How long before Asshur takes you captive?"
versions.explanation: No change to the wording is needed, but a hearer will not know that 'Kain' is another name for the Kenite people just mentioned in v. 21, nor that 'Asshur' is Assyria. A brief footnote (e.g., 'Kain: the Kenites; Asshur: Assyria') would aid comprehension in oral reading.

text: He took up his oracle again and said: "Alas! Who can survive when God does this?
Ships shall come from the coast of Kittim; they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and he too shall come to destruction.

versions.text: Ships shall come from the coast of Cyprus; they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and he too shall come to destruction."
versions.explanation: Place names are handled inconsistently here: 'Asshur' and 'Eber' are kept as Hebrew names, while 'Kittim' is interpreted as 'Cyprus.' Retaining 'Kittim' keeps the oracle's proper names uniform and preserves the wider reference (Cyprus and the western coastlands); an explanatory footnote such as 'Kittim: Cyprus and the coastlands to the west' could be added.

text: Then Balaam got up and went back home, and Balak also went his way.
